articles.title: Veja o que fizeram os candidatos ao governo do AM nesta quarta-feira (9) | G1
articles.standfirst: O primeiro turno será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.
articles.summary: O primeiro turno será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo do Amazonas nas eleições de 2026 participaram de entrevistas e caminhadas nesta quarta-feira (9), em Manaus .

O primeiro turno será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.

Veja abaixo como foi o dia de campanha dos candidatos:

O candidato David Almeida participou de uma entrevista a um portal de notícias na tarde desta quarta-feira (9), em Manaus. Durante a conversa, o candidato afirmou que pretende implantar um programa de asfaltamento de vias no interior do estado.

De manhã, David participou de uma caminhada no bairro Nova Esperança, na Zona Oeste de Manaus. À noite, o candidato finalizou a agenda desta quarta-feira com uma reunião no Mauazinho, Zona Leste de Manaus.

O candidato Omar Aziz participou de uma rodada de entrevistas com candidatos ao governo promovida por uma emissora rádio local, nesta quarta-feira, em Manaus. Ao ser perguntado sobre propostas para geração de renda e criação de empregos na capital e no interior, ele afirmou que têm como foco o desenvolvimento sustentável.

A candidata Professora Maria do Carmo participou de uma entrevista em uma emissora de TV na manhã desta terça-feira (8), em Manaus. Durante a conversa, ela respondeu a perguntas de estudantes e apresentou propostas para melhorar a logística no interior do estado.

A agenda da candidata nesta quarta-feira incluiu ainda outros compromissos na capital amazonense. À tarde, Maria do Carmo realizou gravações para o programa eleitoral. Em seguida, participou de atendimento interno com lideranças da capital.

O candidato Roberto Cidade concedeu entrevista a uma rádio local pela manhã, em Manaus. Durante a tarde, participou de outra entrevista a um portal de notícias, seguida de uma caminhada pela Zona Centro-Oeste da capital. Pela noite, participou de reuniões nas zonas Centro-Oeste, Centro-Sul e Oeste.

O candidato Gilberto Vasconcelos não enviou a agenda de campanha.

O candidato Isael Munduruku reuniu-se com a juventude do conjunto Ouro Verde, em Manaus, durante a manhã. Em seguida, a tarde, realizou panfletagem na feira do Produtor na Zona Leste e visitou apoiadores no bairro Tancredo Neves. De noite, visitou religioso no bairro São José.

O candidato Cabo Daciolo participou de reuniões estratégicas e encerrou o dia retirando-se em oração ao Criador.

articles.title: Kettlebell e anilha de ferro fundido: por que o material importa | G1
articles.standfirst: No treino funcional, o material do kettlebell muda o equilíbrio, a durabilidade e a segurança. Entenda por que o ferro fundido é a referência e como escolher o peso
articles.summary: No treino funcional, o material do kettlebell muda o equilíbrio, a durabilidade e a segurança. Entenda por que o ferro fundido é a referência e como escolher o peso
articles.body:
No treino funcional, o kettlebell parece um peso simples — mas o material de que é feito muda mais do que se imagina. Equilíbrio, durabilidade e segurança dependem de como a peça é fabricada. O ferro fundido virou referência por um motivo: a peça sai inteiriça do molde, sem emendas, com o centro de massa no lugar certo. Vale entender por que isso importa antes de montar o treino em casa.

Kettlebells em ferro fundido: peça inteiriça, com equilíbrio e durabilidade para o treino funcional — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

O kettlebell de ferro fundido é feito de uma peça só , o que garante equilíbrio previsível — essencial nos movimentos balísticos, como o swing, em que a peça gira em torno do punho. Sem emenda ou preenchimento que possa deslocar, o centro de massa fica estável. E o ferro é praticamente indestrutível: aguenta queda no chão do treino sem rachar, como aconteceria com peças ocas ou de cimento.

Peça inteiriça de ferro fundido: centro de massa estável para o swing e resistência à queda no treino.

Iniciantes: comece por pesos moderados e priorize a técnica antes da carga.

Progressão: tenha ao menos duas cargas para alternar exercícios de força e de resistência.

Movimento balístico (swing): exige controle; não comece pesado demais.

Revestimento: modelos emborrachados protegem o piso e reduzem o ruído da queda.

Kettlebells emborrachados em vários pesos: progressão de carga com proteção do piso — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

A progressão pede mais de uma carga. Os kettlebells de ferro fundido vêm em vários pesos, com opção emborrachada. Vale lembrar que a orientação de carga e técnica deve vir de um profissional de educação física.

Sediada em Divinópolis , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, a Panela de Ferro Fundido trabalha com peças de ferro fundido, incluindo linha fitness. Os kettlebells estão no catálogo de kettlebells , com entrega para todo o Brasil.

articles.title: Trump promete dar mais de R$ 25 mil por adulto se republicanos vencerem eleições de novembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA diz que benefício seria pago a todos os cidadãos adultos, desde que o dinheiro seja gasto no país.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA diz que benefício seria pago a todos os cidadãos adultos, desde que o dinheiro seja gasto no país.
articles.body:
Convenção Republicana em Dallas. — Foto: Evan Vucci / Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quarta-feira (9) que pretende conceder um pagamento de US$ 5 mil (cerca de R$ 25.486,50) a cada adulto do país caso os republicanos mantenham o controle da Câmara dos Representantes e do Senado nas eleições de novembro.

O anúncio foi feito durante uma convenção republicana em Dallas, no Texas. Segundo Trump, o benefício seria uma espécie de "dividendo" distribuído aos cidadãos em razão do que classificou como o sucesso da economia americana.

"Se os republicanos vencerem a Câmara dos Representantes e o Senado dos Estados Unidos, ambos... por causa da nossa enorme força e sucesso econômico, vou conceder um dividendo de US$ 5 mil a cada cidadão adulto dos Estados Unidos da América", declarou.

Trump acrescentou que o dinheiro teria uma condição: precisaria ser gasto dentro dos Estados Unidos.

"A única condição é que o dividendo que estamos concedendo seja gasto nos Estados Unidos da América", disse.

O presidente não detalhou como a proposta seria financiada nem quem teria direito ao pagamento. Também não informou quando o benefício seria implementado, caso os republicanos vençam as eleições.

Em novembro, os americanos vão às urnas para as chamadas eleições de meio de mandato, que renovam todos os 435 assentos da Câmara dos Representantes e parte das vagas do Senado. O resultado definirá qual partido controlará o Congresso pelos próximos dois anos, influenciando diretamente a capacidade de Trump de aprovar projetos e avançar sua agenda de governo.

articles.title: Aliados de Trump alertam que guerra com o Irã pode se ir até 2029 | G1
articles.standfirst: Conflito poderia terminar apenas após a posse do próximo presidente dos EUA, em janeiro de 2029. Informações do The Wall Street Journal contrastam com falas de Trump.
articles.summary: Conflito poderia terminar apenas após a posse do próximo presidente dos EUA, em janeiro de 2029. Informações do The Wall Street Journal contrastam com falas de Trump.
articles.body:
Os principais assessores da Casa Branca, incluindo o vice-presidente dos Estados Unidos , JD Vance, e o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, alertaram em particular o presidente Donald Trump de que o conflito com o Irã pode se estender pelo restante do mandato, informou o Wall Street Journal nesta quarta-feira (9), citando autoridades norte-americanas.

Nas discussões privadas no Salão Oval e na Sala de Situação, os assessores disseram a Trump que Teerã poderia continuar resistindo à pressão dos EUA, o que levaria o conflito para além da posse do próximo presidente, em janeiro de 2029, segundo o jornal.

O WSJ informou ainda que assessores de Trump discutem internamente a possibilidade de uma guerra prolongada, enquanto o governo mantém a pressão militar e econômica sobre o Irã.

Segundo o jornal, o Pentágono já estendeu parte da presença de tropas no Oriente Médio para 2027 e prepara novas rotações de forças na região.

O alerta relatado pelo WSJ contrasta com as declarações públicas de Trump sobre a guerra. Nesta quarta-feira, o presidente disse esperar que o conflito termine "imediatamente" após as eleições de meio de mandato dos EUA, em novembro.

Segundo Trump, o Irã estaria tentando influenciar a votação, mas não conseguiria manter a resistência por muito mais tempo.

O presidente também afirmou que as negociações diplomáticas continuam sendo uma possibilidade, embora não sejam a opção preferida.

A Casa Branca não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

articles.title: Operação apreende 3 mil toras de madeira nativa em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Fiscalização também apreendeu nove caminhões e conduziu 15 homens em Brasnorte.
articles.summary: Fiscalização também apreendeu nove caminhões e conduziu 15 homens em Brasnorte.
articles.body:
Quase 3 mil toras de madeira nativa foram apreendidas durante uma operação contra o desmatamento ilegal, em Brasnorte , a 580 km de Cuiabá, nesta segunda-feira (8). Ao todo, 2.863 toras foram encontradas, além de caminhões e outros veículos que, segundo a fiscalização, eram usados para transportar a madeira.

A ação foi realizada pela Secretaria de Estado de Meio Ambiente (Sema), por meio da Coordenadoria de Fiscalização de Flora, com apoio da Força Tática do 1º Comando Regional (CR).

Segundo a Sema, a fiscalização começou após alertas de alta resolução indicarem um ponto de desmatamento na Reserva Indígena Menku . No local, também foi identificada uma estrutura usada para receber, medir, registrar e carregar a madeira.

Conforme a fiscalização, foram encontrados indícios de extração, transporte, armazenamento e comercialização ilegal de madeira nativa.

Durante a operação, 15 homens foram conduzidos. Também foram apreendidos nove caminhões, uma caminhonete, uma picape, uma motocicleta, um trator pá-carregadeira e duas motosserras.

articles.title: Analogue alarm: How synthetic paneer takes a Gondola ride to your plate
articles.summary: Delhi-NCR’s Gondola village drives synthetic (analogue) paneer supply; Haryana bans non-dairy paneer for a year amid failed tests and ongoing raids.
articles.body: Standing outside a closed gate that looks like the entrance to a foundry, the man who identifies himself as Imran asks what we want.“Paneer,” we say. “Do you take large orders?”“Any quantity,” he replies. “We supply to many places in Delhi, Gurgaon and Faridabad. Within a day, we can supply as much paneer as required to Chandigarh.”Imran wasn’t exaggerating. There would be few lives in Delhi-NCR and the vast agglomeration of towns and villages around it that the foundry-like units operating in a cluster here – Gondola village in Nuh’s Punahana block – would not have touched. Their chief produce – synthetic paneer (also analogue or non-dairy) is cheap, lasts a long time, and needs no dairy.Daily, synthetic paneer is delivered in bulk to distributors, mandis, and catering kitchens associated with banquet halls. On the plate, it comes packed into tikkas and stuffed in patties, kulchas, rolls and parathas, and in curries that are lapped up in massive quantities.Synthetic paneer (also analogue or non-dairy) is everywhere. Gondola is among its chief contributors. Last month, Haryana govt banned all forms of non-dairy paneer after finding their presence in a large number of samples tested at labs. But the units that bulk-produce paneer doppelgangers continue to churn out massive batches as orders flow in. The only difference? Gates are shut, and there’s a watch posted outside, just in case a nosy visitor drops by.“Food safety teams are active in the area,” says Imran. At another unit in Punahana city, workers turned abusive when we inquired about paneer production.Gondola specialises in all forms of synthetic paneer, like skimmed milk with palm oil and vegetable fats and soya paste treated mixed milk solids. Over the years, demand for cheap paneer has seen manufacturing units proliferate beyond a single cluster to Katpuri, Punahana city, Bara Bazidpur in Pinangwan, Raniyala and Bodi Kothi in Ferozepur Jhirka and Sheikhpur in Nagina, among other places.They produce quickly, and evidently, do whatever it takes to make their product look the best. “During recent raids on paneer manufacturing units in Punahana, food safety officials found buckets of slaked lime (chuna), which were being used to artificially whiten synthetic paneer,” said a food department source. A ballpark estimate of how much paneer the Gondola belt sends out daily, according to various officials and distributors, these correspondents spoke to, is around 10,000-12,000 kg.Haryana food safety commissioner Manoj Kumar has issued a one-year statewide prohibition under Section 30(2)(a) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, covering analogue or non-dairy paneer, and barring its preparation using milk powder or vegetable oil. Officials have been instructed to seize stocks and initiate criminal prosecution under the FSS Act.Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat, too, have banned synthetic paneer for a year. Sale and production of analogue paneer is not illegal in India as long as it is correctly labelled, but concerns about poor standards and the impact on health have led to a rethink.The state’s latest testing data underlines the scale of the problem: of 285 paneer samples tested between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026, 200 failed to meet standards. In many samples, the Butyrorefractometer (which measures purity) readings and iodine values were significantly beyond limits, showing replacement of natural milk fat with non-milk vegetable fats.Food delivery aggregator platforms are acting too. On Aug 31, Zomato announced a zero-tolerance policy on analogue dishes across its platform. It said restaurant partners have been asked to transition to natural dairy products, remove analogue-dairy items where an immediate switch isn’t feasible, and review supplier product labels and ingredient declarations to ensure accurate menu representation.“Thirteen paneer dairies have been proceeded against by the Nuh regional office. Out of these, three units have already been closed, closure orders have been received against five units, four units are presently under show cause notice, and closure recommendation against one sent to head office,” Nuh deputy commissioner Akhil Pilani said.Who Are The Buyers?A supplier described an organised distribution network connecting Nuh’s manufacturing units with Delhi-NCR’s catering and food businesses. Vehicles, he said, leave early morning carrying “freshly prepared synthetic paneer” to Delhi, Gurgaon and surrounding areas. The economics make the case for synthetic paneer. A commercial buyer paying Rs 340 for a kilogram of full-cream paneer could instead procure the cheapest variety (soya paste and vegetable oils, perhaps with a chuna whitener) for Rs 120-150. For a catering order of 1,000kg, this is a savings of Rs 2 lakh.Sources told TOI synthetic paneer is delivered to distributors at Khandsa Mandi, Subzi Mandi on Gurdwara Road, and Anaj Mandi in Gurgaon and at Janakpuri, Uttam Nagar, and in the east in Delhi, mostly for banquet halls, cloud kitchens and local dairy shops. Hapur, Palwal and Bhiwadi are other centres that produce synthetic paneer for supply to Delhi-NCR.Chef Sunnyy Vyas, also known as Brown Chef India, said texture and taste can offer clues, though they’re no substitute for lab testing. “After spending years in kitchens, you develop an instinct with ingredients,” he said. Good, fresh paneer should break softly and crumble rather than stretch like cheese or rubber, he explained — it typically has a soft, slightly grainy, milky feel and a fresh, milky flavour, whereas analogue products can feel unusually smooth, tight or rubbery, and taste more elastic or processed.But he cautioned this isn’t foolproof. “Some products are made very well and can be difficult to identify without checking the ingredients or doing a proper test.” His message for restaurants using analogue products was simple — transparency. “If they’re using analogue paneer, it should be mentioned clearly on the menu, preferably with the ingredients or what it is made from in brackets.”Is There A Health Impact?Paediatric endocrinologist Dr Ganesh Jevalikar said the concern goes beyond analogue paneer simply being different from the conventional dairy product. “Paneer is commonly consumed as an important source of protein, particularly by vegetarians, but analogue paneer can be deficient in protein because its preparation is fundamentally different and may rely on vegetable fats, palm oil, starches and emulsifiers,” he said.Regular consumption of products high in saturated fat, he added, could contribute to weight gain, obesity and increased LDL cholesterol, with longer-term risks including insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes, particularly when eaten frequently. “The bigger issue is that a low-cost substitute should not be mistaken for a nutritionally equivalent food.”Surabhi Sharma, clinical nutritionist and dietetics at Max Hospital, Gurgaon, said: “The health impact depends on the formulation, serving size and frequency of consumption. Some analogue products can be higher in saturated fat, refined starch, calories and sodium, and lower in protein and calcium than regular dairy paneer. Consistently consuming such foods may therefore result in poorer overall nutrition. There is no scientific proof that properly controlled analogue paneer causes hormonal imbalance, so there is no need for unnecessary panic.”Manpreet Singh, honorary treasurer of National Restaurant Association of India, said good restaurants don’t serve analogue paneer because “that’s against the grain of the business”. “We had a talk organized by FSSAI a few days ago to teach restaurant owners how to maintain standards. Analogue paneer was also discussed, and according to law, you have to state it is analogue. When you’re a decent restaurant, you are charging a particular price. articles.summary: Strong surf across Southern California this weekend blasted through a seawall in Long Beach, caused a massive sinkhole at a celebrity's Malibu home and damag...
articles.body:
To begin to understand how a " super" El Niño winter could punish the Southern California coast, the historic wooden boardwalk on the Long Beach Peninsula may just offer a glimpse at what's to come.

Days of intense waves fueled by Hurricane Marie far away in the Pacific left several sections of the boardwalk destroyed after massive swells swallowed protective sand berms and slammed through the seawall .

That force also left several oceanfront homes damaged, some flooded, with at least 24 homes put under evacuation orders until Wednesday morning, as officials assessed the extent of structural damage from the storm, according to the Long Beach Fire Department.

"The whole beach is gone," said Carmen Vaudry, 58, describing how the sand used to sit just below the boardwalk in front of her home but now appears to have dropped several feet.

But Long Beach wasn't the only victim of the ocean's effortless wrath over the weekend. High surf pounded the region's increasingly fragile coastline from Malibu to San Diego, and experts say it could be only a taste of what is ahead as the El Niño forecast continues to strengthen.

"Unfortunately this is just a preview," University of California climate scientist Daniel Swain said Tuesday during a discussion of the storm . "The coastal flooding later this year … it will get worse this fall and especially this winter."

In Dana Point, relentless waves damaged several beachfront homes, destroying decks and tearing through walls. City officials on Tuesday "red-tagged" seven of those homes in the Capistrano Bay District community, deeming them unsafe for residents, and two others were "yellow-tagged," signifying some safety concerns, according to Dana Point officials.

Farther south in San Clemente, high tides also overran a section of the long-vulnerable coastal railway, once again shutting the route after considerable slope damage and erosion.

The elevated surf also caused a massive sinkhole in the driveway of Nicolas Cage's oceanfront residence in Malibu, leading to the evacuation of 31 homes and a local emergency declaration. Waves also splashed over sections of Pacific Coast Highway near Point Mugu, and in Seal Beach, coastline parking lots flooded .

Much of Southern California's coast remains under advisories for beach hazards or flooding through at least Wednesday night, according to the National Weather Service, which warns that the "combination of high surf and high astronomical tides during the evenings" remains.

"I'm highly concerned," said Matt Taylor, 55, a Peninsula resident who was out Tuesday morning helping clear the street of debris after flooding. "This is just the beginning of the season."

The threat of a strong El Niño has cities racing to do what they can to prepare for even stronger storms that could bring further coastal damage and flooding.

Long Beach officials said they continue to work to fortify the sand berms and seawall that remain, and are checking drains to ensure any flooding can quickly recede.

In Ventura County, public works crews have said they are sending teams out to identify vulnerable coastal locations to see whether they can be strengthened. Orange County has been rehabbing crucial pump stations that can be used if floodwaters threaten neighborhoods. In fire zones such as Pacific Palisades and Altadena, officials are preparing for possible mudflows.

Almost all coastal communities are stockpiling sandbags.

Although an El Niño year doesn't guarantee such storms will develop, the climate pattern tilts the odds in favor of a rainier-than-normal winter across Southern California. Scientists have noted that ocean temperatures are already elevated. That pushes tide lines higher and provides extra energy to storms, possibly meaning even stronger waves. A strong El Niño, as is forecast, could push those elevated ocean temperatures higher.

"We are seeing the effects of El Niño already," said Jonathan Warrick, a research geologist with the U.S. Geological Survey.

Long Beach Peninsula residents told The Times that the ocean often creeps over the seawall and onto the boardwalk — many homes are built to allow water to drain beneath them — but the magnitude of the waves over the weekend, and how close they came to the boardwalk, was something they'd never seen.

Steve Hood, who's lived in the area since the 1960s, said he remembered bigger waves hitting the beach in front of the Peninsula during an El Niño winter in 1997 and 1998, but the storm this Labor Day weekend did more damage.

"We still had quite a bit of beach out there then, so it didn't reach the boardwalk," said Hood, 70. His home isn't oceanfront, so he's not too panicked about the upcoming winter, but he will be prepared for likely flooding, he said.

"It's going to be impactful, no doubt, if it is as severe as they anticipate," he said of El Niño.

Many neighbors are hopeful that the city will proceed with a plan for dredging that would dramatically expand the beach and provide more of a barrier against the waves. Long Beach officials did not respond to questions about that project or its timing, and a website with information has had no updates since last year.

"The city's neglected this for decades," said Taylor, calling it "unprecedented" how close the tide is to the Peninsula's boardwalk. While most residents were able to return to their homes Wednesday morning after evacuations, city officials did yellow-tag one home, deeming it safe only for limited access, according to Long Beach fire spokesperson Capt. Jack Crabtree.

The Long Beach Peninsula is a narrow section of upscale homes with beaches on both sides — one facing Alamitos Bay, the other facing the Pacific Ocean.

That location alone makes it particularly vulnerable for flooding and erosion, but it also sits at a low elevation with a south-facing beach, putting it uniquely at risk for strong southerly swells from tropical storms.

Nearby Seal Beach, just across Alamitos Bay, also contends with many of those preconditions. During an El Niño cycle in 1983, waves collapsed the landmark Seal Beach Pier, which has since been rebuilt.

On the Peninsula in Long Beach on Tuesday, several neighbors checked on one another as they cleaned up debris from the flooding and storm damage.

As one woman retreated to her house, she shouted back to her neighbors: "Peninsula strong!"

Staff writers Rong-Gong Lin II and Karen Garcia contributed to this report.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Outsiders spotted at office, full Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority unit shunted
articles.summary: MMRDA transfers all 16 Social Development Branch staff handling project-affected people (PAP) rehabilitation after inspection found procedural lapses and unauthorised persons.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has ordered a wholesale change of its Social Development Branch, transferring all 16 officials and employees — from the deputy collector to peons — after Metropolitan commissioner Sanjay Mukherjee’s surprise inspection of the unit handling rehabilitation and housing for project-affected people (PAPs) .The move follows the detection of procedural lapses and the presence of unauthorised persons on the branch premises by Mukherjee during his inspection.He subsequently directed officials to undertake a detailed review of the branch’s functioning and strengthen administrative supervision and controls.Following the review, MMRDA decided to undertake a complete administrative restructuring of the branch.Employees working at different levels have been transferred and fresh responsibilities assigned for handling PAP cases, maintaining records, scrutinising applications and processing cases for further action.The deputy collector handling PAP-related matters, including cases linked to Metro projects, has also been transferred as part of the reshuffle.The branch plays a crucial role in facilitating rehabilitation housing for people displaced or affected by major infrastructure projects. It also processes applications and related documentation of eligible PAPs before allotment and other rehabilitation measures are undertaken.Given the sensitivity of PAP-related matters, the MMRDA administration has stressed the need for the process to remain transparent, properly documented and free from intermediaries.The presence of unauthorised persons in such a unit has therefore prompted the authority to tighten oversight.The wholesale transfers are being viewed as a significant administrative intervention aimed at strengthening accountability and ensuring that project-affected families get a more transparent and direct mechanism for pursuing their rehabilitation claims.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.summary: Maharashtra SIR drive: Nalasopara tops unmapped voters (1,04,747), Panvel second and Hadapsar third; voters can upload documents online via CEO website using EPIC/OTP.
articles.body: PUNE: Amravati’s Badnera (1.23 lakh), Pune’s Hadapsar (1.22 lakh), Thane’s Ovala Majiwada (1.18 lakh) and Mumbai’s Malad West (1.11 lakh) are among the 15 assembly constituencies in Maharashtra with the maximum discrepancies in the SIR list.Interestingly voters in three constituencies in Nagpur are set to receive over a lakh notices, including Nagpur North (1.08 lakh), Nagpur East (1.07 lakh) and Nagpur West (1.07 lakh).Notices are being issued to voters whose forms were not mapped to the earlier electoral roll as well as those whose enumeration forms reported anomalies or discrepancies (details including name, age, address) compared to those on the electoral roll.The assembly constituency of Badnera in Amravati has reported 1.08 lakh voters with anomalies, the highest in the state.The other constituencies with a large number of voters with anomalies include Kamthi in Nagpur (66,964), Nagpur North (61,248), Nalasopara in Palghar (55,875), Solapur South (50,978) and Malad West (49,703).The Nalasopara constituency has reported 1.04 lakh unmapped electors, highest in the state. This is followed by Hadapsar in Pune (85,853), Thane’s Ovala Majiwada (75,808) and Kalyan rural (71,544), Pune’s Khadakwasala (65,708) and Thane’s Airoli (65,180).Across the state, 62.5 lakh electors on the draft SIR roll have been reported with anomalies and 59.7 lakh are unmapped.Experts said the concentration in urban and rapidly expanding belts reflects higher population mobility and address changes, and expanding areas are witnessing a large number of unmapped voters, especially in the urban pockets.So far, 2 crore voters in the state were excluded in the SIR draft roll. Now another 1.2 crore voters will receive notices for documents and face scrutiny. As a result, the number of exclusions may increase.Electors on the draft list who will receive notices because their forms are unmapped or have anomalies, will have until Oct 29 to respond and provide the documents.Those in the unmapped category will have to provide proof of themselves or their relatives being part of the 2002-04 electoral roll through one of the 11 documents listed by the Election Commission of India. The final electoral roll of the SIR in the state will be published on Nov 4.A senior election official said the process of submitting documents addressing anomalies has been made simpler. articles.title: ED searches Karnataka minister Satish Jarkiholi, daughter  over sugar, Africa biz deals
articles.summary: ED raids 18 premises linked to Karnataka minister Satish Jarkiholi and MP Priyanka; FEMA probe examines forex flows tied to sugar, mining and Africa ventures.
articles.body: BENGALURU/BELAGAVI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Wednesday carried out simultaneous searches at 18 premises linked to Karnataka PWD minister Satish Jarkiholi, his daughter and Chikkodi MP Priyanka Jarkiholi, and their associates across Karnataka and neighbouring Maharashtra.The multi-city crackdown was a fresh investigation, reportedly under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) and not linked to any ongoing money-laundering case involving Manjunath.Belagavi district, home turf of the Jarkiholi family, served as a major focal point of the ED searches, with officials deployed at seven key locations across Belagavi city and Gokak taluk.Simultaneous searches were also conducted at the 64-year-old minister’s residence in Dollars’ Colony and his official quarters on Crescent Road in Bengaluru. While minister Satish Jarkiholi was at his Bengaluru residence, his daughter Priyanka was in Belagavi.Investigators are scrutinising foreign exchange flows allegedly linked to sugar industries, mining ventures and commercial projects in African countries, particularly Rwanda and Uganda.ED teams arrived early in the morning at the minister’s primary family residence, where Priyanka was present during the operation. Officials also searched the Gokak premises of Vitthal Parasannavar and Raju Dharnatti, both known close aides of the minister.In Belagavi city, the teams searched the Laxmi Tekdi residence and Club Road office of Dr Girish Sonwalkar, as well as the Kumaraswamy Layout residence of former KPCC member Malagouda Patil.ED teams also searched, for the second time, the residence of Y Manjunath, the minister’s brother-in-law and an additional commissioner in the excise department.ED sources clarified that while earlier probes involving the state excise department had focused on family members, the present action is an independent investigation tracing suspected money trails linked to overseas entities.The searches triggered a political backlash in Karnataka, with Congress leaders alleging that central agencies were being used to target the state govt and its leaders.Defending his brother, MLC Lakhan Jarkiholi said Satish had several independent business interests, including sugar mills and overseas ventures, and would cooperate fully with the investigation and provide documents to establish the legitimacy of his assets and business dealings.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.summary: O concurso da Câmara de Trindade oferece 11 vagas para diversos níveis de escolaridade, com inscrições abertas até outubro e salários de até R$ 2,5 mil.
articles.body:
Câmara Municipal de Trindade-PE — Foto: Divulgação/ Redes Sociais

A Câmara Municipal de Trindade , no Sertão de Pernambuco, está com inscrições abertas para um novo concurso público. O processo seletivo oferece 11 vagas imediatas para cargos de diferentes níveis de escolaridade.

Os interessados podem se inscrever até o dia 8 de outubro de 2026, exclusivamente pela internet, no site do Instituto IBED , responsável pela organização do certame. A taxa de inscrição varia de R$ 80 a R$ 110, dependendo do nível de escolaridade do cargo pretendido.

Os cargos são para Analista Contábil (1 vaga), Técnico de Controle Interno (1 vaga), Auxiliar de Secretaria (1 vaga), Auxiliar Administrativo (4 vagas de ampla concorrência + 1 vaga PCD), Agente de Segurança (1 vaga) e Auxiliar de Serviços Gerais (2 vagas)

As remunerações variam de R$ 1.621,00 a R$ 2.500,00, de acordo com a função escolhida. A jornada de trabalho exigida é de 30 horas semanais para todos os cargos.

A seleção dos candidatos será feita por meio de uma prova objetiva, prevista para ser aplicada no dia 29 de novembro de 2026, para todos os inscritos. Haverá também uma prova de títulos, de caráter classificatório, destinada apenas aos concorrentes de nível superior.

A divulgação do resultado final está prevista para o dia 29 de janeiro de 2027. O concurso público terá validade de um ano, contado a partir da data de homologação do resultado, podendo ser prorrogado por igual período.

articles.title: Como imprensa internacional noticiou novo capítulo da guerra no STF | G1
articles.standfirst: A agência Bloomberg noticiou que Edson Fachin tomou as medidas 'mais agressivas até o momento' em sua tentativa de retomar o controle do STF.
articles.summary: 'Pior crise desde a redemocratização': agência Bloomberg noticiou que Edson Fachin tomou as medidas 'mais agressivas até o momento' em sua tentativa de retomar o controle do STF.
articles.body:
Decisões de Edson Fachin foram notícia na imprensa internacional — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A imprensa internacional voltou a noticiar a crise no Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) após um dia que viu diversas reviravoltas, com decisões sendo anunciadas e revertidas.

Na quarta-feira (9), o presidente do STF , Edson Fachin, anunciou uma série de medidas para debelar a crise provocada pelo escândalo do Banco Master . O presidente decidiu:

derrubar os efeitos da decisão do ministro André Mendonça , que havia afastado o diretor da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues;

suspender a decisão do ministro Flávio Dino , que havia reintegrado Rodrigues ao cargo;

retirar o inquérito das Fake News da relatoria do ministro Alexandre de Moraes e assumir ele próprio a condução das investigações;

paralisar o andamento da petição de Mendonça que questiona a conduta de Moraes, até nova decisão;

convocar uma sessão plenária para o dia 15 de setembro.

A agência Bloomberg noticiou que "essas medidas são as mais agressivas de Fachin até o momento em sua tentativa de retomar o controle de uma corte que mergulhou em sua crise mais profunda desde o retorno do Brasil à democracia, quatro décadas atrás".

"Essa saga ameaça transformar a iminente eleição presidencial em um referendo sobre os amplos poderes da Corte, com o embate entre Moraes e Mendonça refletindo uma polarização política mais ampla às vésperas de uma eleição que coloca frente a frente o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador de direita Flávio Bolsonaro."

Sobre Alexandre de Moraes , a Bloomberg escreve que "seus esforços agressivos para combater a desinformação fizeram dele o principal antagonista de conservadores como o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro ". A agência afirma que ele se transformou no juiz mais famoso do Brasil.

Já Mendonça é descrito como um dos críticos mais ferrenhos de Moraes dentro do tribunal e "um dos membros mais poderosos da corte desde fevereiro, quando assumiu a supervisão da investigação sobre o Banco Master".

Sobre o inquérito das fake news, a agência escreve que ele se expandiu "para uma investigação de amplo alcance que transformou Moraes em um dos principais alvos de polêmica política no Brasil, à medida que ele entrava em confronto com gigantes das redes sociais e políticos de direita de destaque, incluindo o bilionário Elon Musk e o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro ".

As decisões de Fachin também foram divulgadas por outras agências de notícias.

A AP noticiou que "a disputa de poder na Suprema Corte também causou danos à própria instituição , com críticos condenando veementemente o caos que a abala em suas bases".

"A divergência entre os ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal, percebidos como ocupando extremos opostos do espectro político brasileiro, está se tornando uma questão importante às vésperas da eleição presidencial do mês que vem", afirma a agência.

A Reuters também noticiou que o embate entre os ministros "lançou a mais alta corte do Brasil em sua maior crise desde o retorno do país à democracia, há mais de quatro décadas".

"As instituições brasileiras estão sendo abaladas pela ampliação das investigações sobre o Banco Master e por supostos vínculos entre o presidente do banco, Daniel Vorcaro, e autoridades do governo e políticos da oposição."

Na quarta-feira, após a ordem do ministro Flávio Dino de reintegrar o diretor da Polícia Federal — mas antes da decisão de Fachin anulando essa e outras ordens — o jornal argentino Clarín noticiou que o Brasil vive uma "guerra aberta entre os juízes da Suprema Corte do Brasil em plena campanha eleitoral".

"As disputas internas continuam a aumentar no Supremo Tribunal Federal do Brasil, em um confronto sem precedentes entre seus juízes em meio a uma campanha eleitoral."

articles.title: Can husband be tried for marital rape if law says not offence: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Citing Article 20(1) of the Constitution which shields persons from prosecution for an act which is not an offence under existing penal law.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Citing Article 20(1) of the Constitution which shields persons from prosecution for an act which is not an offence under existing penal laws, the Supreme Court on Wednesday asked whether a husband can be prosecuted for marital rape when the law categorically states that it is not an offence, even as it agreed with the Centre that the matter should be left for Parliament’s consideration.Article 20(1) provides that “no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of law in force at that time…” Section 375(2) of IPC said “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being under 15 years, is not rape” (wife’s age was raised to 18 by SC in 2017), with the provision replicated in Sect 63(2) of BNS.Centre should go back to drawing board if law has a problem, says SCWith a bunch of petitions challenging the constitutional validity of this exception to rape, a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the matter posed foundational questions, especially citing the case in which a husband has challenged a Karnataka high court decision to permit his prosecution for marital rape.The hearing saw Solicitor General Tushar Mehta arguing that the issue, given its complexity, be left for the Parliament to consider.It will be absurd for courts to take upon themselves the task of determining the nature of sex — natural or unnatural — when it is best left to people, their representatives and legislature, SG Tushar Mehta said.The bench agreed. “It should always come from Parliament. If the govt feels there is a problem with the law, then it should go back to the drawing board and recast the law with approval of Parliament,” it said.During the last hearing, SC had wondered whether the court can rewrite penal laws to create a new offence.Senior advocate Karuna Nundy said that no new offence needs to be created as the offence of rape is already defined and the only question is whether it is constitutionally justified to grant immunity from it to a class of persons (husbands).Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India’s push for agreement at the BRICS summit beginning Sept 12 faces divisions among its members over the West Asia conflict.Russian offi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s push for agreement at the BRICS summit beginning Sept 12 faces divisions among its members over the West Asia conflict.Russian officials, speaking to their country’s media, have acknowledged difficult negotiations, while Brazilian reporting has raised doubts about a strong final declaration. Yet Chinese commentary has highlighted opportunities for India’s presidency, including closer trade ties. These contrasting accounts suggest that the challenge for New Delhi is to keep economic cooperation moving while finding language that countries with conflicting security interests can accept.The Sept 12–13 summit at Bharat Mandapam will bring these differences into focus. A final declaration records the common positions that participating countries have agreed to support.Cannot predict outcome of declaration: Russian ministerRussian deputy foreign minister Sergey Ryabkov told TASS that some members were sharply critical of Tehran’s actions, making the Gulf situation Brics’ most pressing political issue. “And as of today, I cannot predict what the outcome will be,” he said about negotiations on the final document.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov acknowledged that Iran–UAE differences complicated drafting, but expressed confidence that diplomats would find acceptable wording.The disagreement concerns what members want Brics to say about the conflict. Iran’s Mehr agency reported its judiciary chief’s call at a preparatory meeting for condemnation of US–Israeli attacks. UAE agency WAM highlighted Emirati criticism of Iranian attacks on commercial shipping and demands to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.Chinese commentary has focused on India’s economic strengths. A Global Times article carried by People’s Daily praised its strengths in digital techn and medicine, while saying that bridging differences among members would test Indian diplomacy.Another Global Times commentary advocated deeper India–China trade and greater Chinese market access for Indian products. Indian reporting has highlighted New Delhi’s concerns about Chinese restrictions on critical technologies and industrial components.In Brazil, CNN Brasil reported that President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva would prioritise poll campaigning and send foreign minister Mauro Vieira. South Africa’s Business Day questioned whether expansion had weakened Brics’ unity, while broadcaster SABC highlighted Pretoria’s push for trade, industrialisation and African infra investment.For India, success would mean reaching useful agreements on specific issues while negotiating a common political message among partners whose interests do not always coincide.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Satya Niketan building collapse: PG operator ran 7 such facilities in same area
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has arrested the man who used to run a PG facility on four floors of the building that collapsed in Satya Niketan under the na.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has arrested the man who used to run a PG facility on four floors of the building that collapsed in Satya Niketan under the name Hostel Daze.Police suspect he runs a total of seven such facilities in the area under the same name and are probing his entire operation. This building collapsed on Sept 6, leaving seven people dead.The operator, Shudhanshu Lovneesh (31) has told cops that he had taken four floors in the ill-fated building on lease, along with associate Shubham Tyagi, in Aug last year for Rs 1.05 lakh per month. Tyagi is absconding.They managed to rent the building cheap due to its dilapidated condition.PG operator fled after students identified himA resident of Bhajanpura, Lovneesh graduated from Delhi University in 2019, and three years later, in 2022, he and Tyagi got into the business of running PG accommodations in Satya Niketan. He has told the cops that there are several others like him who are operating such facilities in old buildings on lease.A Delhi court Wednesday remanded Lovneesh and two others - building owner's son Mahesh Gupta (52) and contractor Sanoj - in two days in police custody. Mahesh was produced after his earlier two-day police remand ended. Police had sought three days' custody for all three to question them and confront them with the owner of the building, Hariram Gupta (81) who retired from IAF, and his wife, Urmila (75) who had been sent to 14 days in judicial custody Monday.Contractor Sanoj has told the cops that the basement was getting flooded with rainwater for 8 to 10 days and, in an unconventional solution, had been filled with three truckloads of construction debris to bring it up to the level of the ground floor.Police Wednesday confirmed TOI's report that the building collapsed like a pack of cards because a retaining wall on the ground floor was removed to merge two shops. Four additional floors had already been built on a weak foundation and the removal of the wall was the last straw.Sanoj told the police that he had been engaged for the work by Mahesh Gupta around 10 days before the incident and was being paid Rs 2,800 per day. He had been apprehended from Kasganj in UP on Tuesday. The labourers engaged in the work were being paid Rs 800 daily and they too are being questioned.Police sources said Lovneesh had reached the spot soon after the building collapsed but fled after students began to point him out as the operator of the PG. He then rushed to a friend's house in Burari, from where the police have nabbed him.The proceedings for remand of Lovneesh, Mahesh Gupta and Sanoj in the court of judicial magistrate Kautuk Bharadwaj were held in camera after the counsel for Lovneesh said the case was at a nascent stage and a "media trial" would prejudice the ongoing probe. articles.title: ‘Lal Mandir was original target’: How traffic forced Red Fort bomber to change plans
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: On Nov 10 last year, 13 minutes before the explosive-laden i20 exploded near Red Fort, bomber Umar-un-Nabi tried to park the car near ‘Lal .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: On Nov 10 last year, 13 minutes before the explosive-laden i20 exploded near Red Fort, bomber Umar-un-Nabi tried to park the car near ‘Lal Mandir’ in Chandni Chowk — suggesting it was the first target — but was diverted due to heavy traffic and police presence there. CCTV footage captured him attempting to park at 6.37pm, after which he took a U-turn and reached near Gate No. 4 of Red Fort, where he triggered the IED at 6.50pm.The details are part of the chargesheet recently filed by National Investigation Agency (NIA) in connection with the Red Fort blast. The chargesheet provides extensive details of the planning and execution of the first-ever vehicle-borne IED (VBIED) attack reported in the national capital.NIA has said the VBIED was detonated through a remote ‘command mechanism’ fitted in one of the shoes of the bomber, Umar-un-Nabi. A metal piece attached to the heel of one shoe was found adjacent to the i20 used by Umar, and it tested positive for triacetone triperoxide (TATP), potassium and ammonium nitrate. The other exhibits from this car included a nasal orifice swab matched with the DNA of Umar’s parents, confirming his identity as the bomber, the chargesheet stated.Further, a forensic report of the blast reported in Nowgam, J&K, on the explosives seized from Umar’s associates from Faridabad also tested positive for the same chemicals, confirming the module’s existence.“The yield (impact) of TATP and its stability also depends on its storage in a cold environment and presence of 10% water. Witnesses have deposed that Umar used to keep his room extremely cool, and that a foul smell used to emanate from it. He and others had also purchased collapsible water bags, which were used to keep the prepared TATP under wet conditions to keep it safe. Water was regularly added to the IED to keep the explosive mixture stable,” the chargesheet said.The post-mortem reports of the victims furnished by the hospital ascertain the cause of death to be “high-intensity blast wave effect”. The blast, the chargesheet said, led to the death of 11 people and injuries to 29. Damage to the nearby structures amounted to Rs 17.7 lakh, as assessed by authorities like DMRC, ASI and PWD, it added.NIA found that on Oct 30, Umar met an acquaintance behind Al Falah hospital, gave him his room key and asked him to bring his “shoes” from the almirah in the room. “He was already wearing his shoes at the time. He was visibly distressed as J&K police had raided the module by then,” said the chargesheet.While on the run, Umar was storing his urine in a polythene bag, as observed by the woman who owned the house in Nuh where he had sought shelter. “He did not go outside to dispose of it and thus a foul smell was emanating from the room, prompting the woman to complain to her husband,” the chargesheet said.“Interestingly, an innovative method for preparing explosive substances using urea nitrate has been elaborated in a PDF material seized from the pen drives of the accused wherein an alternative method for the source of urea is mentioned as — ‘extracting urea from urine’.”It also mentioned the seizure of a terror manual, “Lone Mujahid Pocket Book”, which was published in “Inspire” magazine, affiliated with Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), being followed by the module. NIA said the manual provided operational information related to explosives, weapons, vehicles, arson and covert activities, with detailed chapters on TATP and remote-control mechanisms for detonating IEDs.On Nov 7, Umar also bought a new T-shirt, a wine-coloured shirt and green-coloured cargo pants by making payment in cash to a shop in Nuh, the chargesheet said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump turned his Republican Party’s midterm convention in Dallas into a showcase for his trademark political rhetoric on Wednesday.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump turned his Republican Party’s midterm convention in Dallas into a showcase for his trademark political rhetoric on Wednesday, suggesting the Strait of Hormuz should be renamed the “Trump Strait” as he sought to rally voters behind the GOP ahead of the November elections.“I think we should call the Hormuz Strait the Trump Strait. I should get something out of it. The Trump Strait,” Trump told the crowd, referring to the strategically vital waterway amid heightened tensions with Iran.Trump also renewed his pitch for renaming Lake Ontario claiming that the water body should be called “Lake America” and suggesting New Mexico could become “New America”. “Canada very much wants to make a deal. They're dying to make a deal. But it's going to be called Lake America,” he said.The remarks came as Trump used his keynote address to make a broader pitch for Republican candidates and his administration’s record. He urged supporters to treat the upcoming midterms as though he himself were on the ballot, despite not being eligible to seek another presidential term.“If we hand America’s future to the radical-left Democrats, our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet,” Trump said. “Vote Republican and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come.”Trump said there were around 35 key Senate and House races and pledged to campaign across the states involved, promising, “We’re gonna have rallies just like this.”He also highlighted his administration’s tax policies, including “No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, and No Tax on Social Security”, while claiming that the US had attracted more than $20 trillion in foreign investment.“This has been the most successful two years financially and every other way in the history of the presidency,” Trump said.The president also defended Senate Majority Leader John Thune after the Texas crowd booed him, saying, “No, no. articles.title: Spain released wild horses into the Iberian Highlands after a 10,000-year absence; the animals are being used to rebuild a fire-prone landscape
articles.summary: Europe News: Przewalski’s horses are roaming Spain’s Iberian Highlands again after an absence of more than 10,000 years, as a rewilding project uses the animals’ n.
articles.body: Przewalski’s horses are roaming Spain’s Iberian Highlands again after an absence of more than 10,000 years, as a rewilding project uses the animals’ natural grazing to reshape a landscape increasingly vulnerable to wildfires. The horses were released in Villanueva de Alcorón, Guadalajara province, as part of an effort by Rewilding Spain to restore the ecological role once played by large wild herbivores. Their grazing and trampling reduce vegetation and forest biomass, while helping create a more varied landscape of woodland and open pasture. The return of the horses follows their near-extinction in the 20th century and represents a new stage in efforts to restore natural processes across the Iberian Highlands. According to Rewilding Spain, an environmental conservation initiative, the animals can help improve pasture quality and support biodiversity, while reducing the amount of combustible vegetation. The project is an opportunity for visitors to observe horses living freely in Western Europe.Spain’s wild horses rebuild a fire-prone landscapeThe horses are not being released simply to increase the number of wild animals in the region. Their grazing is intended to replace an ecological function that was lost after extensive livestock farming, with horses and cattle disappearing from parts of the Alto Tajo. As the animals feed and move through the landscape, they reduce vegetation and forest biomass while creating more varied pasture conditions.Rewilding Spain says natural grazing by large herbivores is important for restoring healthy ecosystems because feeding and trampling can reduce the amount of forest biomass available. The organisation states that the horses “reduce forest biomass available in the area”, while their grazing also improves the diversity and quality of pastures used by deer, roe deer, fallow deer and domestic sheep and goats.Wild horses create a natural firebreakThe Iberian Highlands have extensive areas of forest and vegetation where a lack of large grazers can allow shrubs and other plants to become denser. Rewilding Spain is using natural grazing as one way of changing that vegetation structure. By eating grasses, shrubs and other plants and moving through the landscape, the horses help create more open areas and a mixture of different vegetation types.The wider rewilding initiative explicitly links this work with wildfire prevention. Horses can help make landscapes more heterogeneous and richer in terms of biodiversity, which it considers important for reducing vulnerability to wildfires. Its Iberian Highlands programme also says horses are helping to open up areas affected by past fires, increasing structural diversity and creating a landscape mosaic that can support regeneration.Wild horses expand large-herbivore grazing in SpainThe return of Przewalski’s horses is also part of a wider programme to restore large-herbivore grazing across the Iberian Highlands. Rewilding Spain is working with Przewalski’s horses alongside Serrano and Pottoka horses and tauros cattle in different parts of the landscape. The organisation says the combined management of large herbivores now covers tens of thousands of hectares, to support forest regeneration, biodiversity and wildfire prevention.The horses are also becoming part of the region’s nature-tourism economy. Their presence has already attracted visitors to Villanueva de Alcorón, where guided trips allow people to see the animals living independently in the landscape.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bali tour never conducted after payment; Kerala panel orders Rs 1.12 lakh payout
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed a travel agency to refund Rs 82,500 to a customer after finding deficiency in service.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed a travel agency to refund Rs 82,500 to a customer after finding deficiency in service and unfair trade practice over its failure to conduct a Bali tour or return the money for several years. The commission also awarded Rs 25,000 for mental agony, inconvenience and hardship and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. The order was passed on August 31, 2026.Why did the customer approach the commission?According to the commission order, the customer booked a three-night, four-day Bali tour package with Kerala Travel Zone after seeing its advertisements on social media. He paid Rs 60,000 on December 23, 2019, followed by Rs 22,500 on December 26, taking the total payment to Rs 82,500.The proposed tour could not be conducted because of the Covid-19 pandemic. The customer said that after international travel resumed, he repeatedly approached the travel agency either to conduct the tour or refund his money.According to him, the agency kept postponing the journey and eventually informed him that the tour would be conducted on December 28, 2022. The journey was later rescheduled to April 10, 2023, but the tour was not conducted even then.The customer subsequently sent a lawyer notice demanding a refund of Rs 82,500 along with compensation. Although the agency received the notice, it neither replied nor refunded the money.The customer told the commission that the agency's conduct caused him financial loss, inconvenience, mental agony and disappointment.The travel agency and its proprietor did not appear before the commission despite receiving notices and were proceeded against ex parte.What did the commission find about the travel agency's conduct?The bench comprising president C.T. Sabu and members Sreeja S. and Ram Mohan R. noted that the customer's bank statements established payment of Rs 82,500 and that the agency itself had issued a letter regarding rescheduling of the proposed journey.The commission said the customer's documentary evidence remained unchallenged because the opposite parties chose not to contest the complaint.“In ex parte proceedings, though the burden initially lies upon the complainant, once reliable documentary evidence is produced and the same remains unchallenged, there is absolutely no reason to disbelieve such evidence,” the commission held.It said the Covid-19 pandemic had prevented international tours during the relevant period, but after restrictions were lifted and international tourism resumed, the agency was required either to conduct the agreed tour or refund the money within a reasonable time.“Instead of adopting either course, the opposite parties repeatedly postponed the journey and continued to retain the complainant's money for several years without rendering any service whatsoever. Retention of a consumer's money for years together without providing the promised service clearly amounts to deficiency in service within the meaning of Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019,” the commission said.The commission also found that repeatedly postponing the tour after taking the package amount amounted to an unfair trade practice.“Further, inducing consumers to pay the package amount by advertising tour packages and thereafter continuously postponing the service without refunding the consideration also amounts to an unfair trade practice as contemplated under Section 2(47) of the Act,” it held.The commission noted that the pandemic was beyond the travel agency's control when the original cancellation occurred, but said its subsequent failure to conduct the tour or refund the money was unjustified.It directed the travel agency and its proprietor to jointly and severally refund Rs 82,500 with 9 percent annual interest from the date of filing of the complaint until realization. It also awarded Rs 25,000 as compensation for mental agony, inconvenience and hardship and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.The total payout comes to Rs 1,12,500, apart from the interest on the refund. The amounts have to be paid within 45 days of receipt of the order. If there is a default, the compensation amount will also carry 9 percent annual interest from the date of default until realization.

articles.title: In 2019, a Norfolk farm began giving 500 acres of marginal farmland back to nature; three years later, average plant diversity had doubled and ex-arable plots rose from 7 to 32 species
articles.summary: UK News: When Wild Ken Hill, a coastal farm in Norfolk, began transforming 500 acres of poor, marginal farmland in 2019, the aim was to let nature recover with.
articles.body: When Wild Ken Hill, a coastal farm in Norfolk, began transforming 500 acres of poor, marginal farmland in 2019, the aim was to let nature recover with as little intervention as possible. Three years later, a repeat vegetation survey found that the average number of plant species in open parts of the rewilding area had almost doubled, from 16.8 in 2019 to 33.2 in 2022. The findings, published by the farm and supported by independent conservation bodies including Rewilding Britain, offer an early glimpse of how quickly biodiversity can respond when former farmland is given space to recover.From farmland to a landscape shaped by natureThe Wild Ken Hill project began taking shape in January 2019. Alongside rewilding 500 acres of marginal farmland and a similar area of woodland, the estate began restoring its freshwater marshes and shifting the rest of its agricultural operation towards regenerative farming focused on soil health.The rewilding area was managed through natural grazing, with free-roaming Red Poll cattle, Exmoor ponies and Tamworth pigs helping shape the vegetation. Beavers were later introduced as ecosystem engineers, while the site continued to be monitored through detailed ecological surveys.The project now combines three approaches: rewilding, traditional conservation and regenerative agriculture. Rewilding Britain describes the site as a 416-hectare project that began in 2019 and includes lowland grassland and woodland.Plant diversity almost doubles in three yearsThe most striking results came from a vegetation survey repeated in 2022 by naturalist Graeme Lyons, who had established a baseline in 2019. Across open parts of the rewilding area, the average number of plant species recorded per plot rose from 16.8 to 33.2. But the change was even more dramatic in areas that had previously been cultivated fields.There, the average number of plant species increased from about seven to around 32, more than a fourfold rise. The survey covered 57 plots that had previously been used for arable farming, conservation margins or grassland. Researchers returned to the same locations using GPS and recorded vegetation using the same methodology, allowing changes over time to be compared.One particularly striking sandy-soil plot went from just four plant species in 2019 to 48 three years later. Species such as Common Cudweed and Smooth Cat’s-ear became much more abundant. The survey also recorded an increase in seedlings, from 651 in 2019 to 1,075 in 2022, suggesting that natural regeneration of scrub and trees was beginning to take place.Why grazing animals matterThe results also underline that rewilding does not necessarily mean simply leaving land untouched. At Wild Ken Hill, grazing animals have played an important role in changing the structure of vegetation. Their grazing, trampling and movement create openings and variation in the landscape, helping some plants establish while preventing others from dominating.But the survey also revealed an important caveat. Areas that were already relatively species-rich, including some former conservation margins and grassland, did not improve as dramatically as the former arable fields. That has led the project to consider “pulsed” grazing, allowing sections of land to rest for periods before animals return. The idea is to create cycles of disturbance and recovery rather than subjecting the entire area to continuous grazing.More plants could mean more wildlifeThe significance of the changes goes beyond the plants themselves. The 2022 survey found that both the abundance and diversity of nectar sources had increased. That could provide additional food for insects, with potential knock-on effects for species higher up the food chain, including birds and bats.The survey also found an increase in the average number of plant species with conservation status, although the change was partly driven by the spread of particular species rather than a uniform increase across every plot. That distinction matters. The results do not suggest that every part of the site improved in exactly the same way. Instead, they show how different starting conditions can produce very different outcomes, and why long-term monitoring is crucial to understanding rewilding.A longer experiment is now underwayWild Ken Hill’s experience is therefore less a simple story of “leave farmland alone and biodiversity returns” than an experiment in how natural processes can be restored on former agricultural land.The estate continues to combine rewilding with regenerative farming and active conservation of its wetlands. The site’s wider approach has also included the reintroduction of beavers, which have created dams and altered wetland habitats.For now, the biggest lesson from the first three years is visible at ground level: fields that once produced crops such as sugar beet and spring barley were, in places, becoming increasingly varied plant communities. The transformation is still in its early stages. But the jump from seven plant species to around 32 on former arable plots suggests that, given the right conditions, nature can begin rewriting a landscape much faster than might be expected.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet James Taylor, the 14-year-old Welsh football freestyler who taught himself on YouTube, set five Guinness World Records and finished third at a world championship
articles.summary: UK News: At 14, James Taylor has already made a name for himself on the international football freestyle circuit. The teenager from Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan,.
articles.body: At 14, James Taylor has already made a name for himself on the international football freestyle circuit. The teenager from Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, recently finished third at the NextGen World Football Freestyle Championships in the Netherlands, adding another achievement to a remarkable record-breaking run. BBC Wales reported on his latest podium finish, while Italian youth publication Focus Junior has also highlighted his five Guinness World Records and success at the championships. Taylor is self-taught, developing his skills through daily practice and by studying football freestyle tutorials on YouTube. His latest Guinness World Record came in April 2026, when he set the under-16 record for the most “around-the-world” ball-control tricks in one minute.From YouTube tutorials to world recordsUnlike traditional football, freestyle football focuses on individual ball control, tricks and creative combinations rather than scoring goals against an opponent. For Taylor, much of that learning happened independently.His record-breaking journey began while he was still a young aspiring freestyler. Guinness World Records records Taylor completing 77 football shoulder rolls in one minute in Cardiff in November 2023. He later set a record for 6,023 consecutive alternating football rebounder volleys in July 2024. In April 2024, he also completed 95 football “hotstepper” ball-control tricks in one minute in Penarth.His latest record came in front of thousandsTaylor’s most recent Guinness World Record was set on April 11, 2026, at Cardiff City Football Club. In front of a crowd of 21,640 during half-time at Cardiff City’s match against Bolton Wanderers, he completed 76 “around the world” ball-control tricks in one minute in the under-16 category. Guinness World Records lists the achievement as the current record for the most such tricks in one minute by an under-16.The move requires a player to repeatedly circle a foot around the football before regaining control of it, making speed, balance and concentration crucial. Taylor’s record collection also includes another shoulder-roll achievement: Guinness records him completing 41 football shoulder rolls in 30 seconds in Penarth in December 2025.Third place on the world stageHis latest success came not in a record attempt but in competition. Taylor travelled to the Netherlands for the NextGen World Football Freestyle Championships, where he finished third against other young freestyle footballers. BBC Wales reported that the result further established him among the leading freestyle performers in his age group.The achievement is particularly notable given how Taylor developed his skills. Rather than coming through a conventional football academy focused on match play, he has built his freestyle ability through self-directed training and online instruction.His progress also reflects how platforms such as YouTube have become training grounds for young athletes pursuing highly specialised skills that may not be widely taught in conventional sporting environments.A teenager turning practice into precisionTaylor’s story is less about a single spectacular trick than the thousands of repetitions behind it. His routine of practising every day and learning from online videos has taken him from experimenting with freestyle football to competing internationally and appearing in the Guinness World Records database multiple times.At 14, he now has five world records and a world-championship podium finish to his name. And with freestyle football continuing to give young players a competitive stage of their own, Taylor’s next challenge may simply be finding another record that he can break.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In Gateshead, water trapped 150 metres below the city in abandoned coal mines now heats 350 homes and public buildings
articles.summary: UK News: Water trapped deep beneath Gateshead is now helping heat hundreds of homes and public buildings, turning former coal mine workings into a source of he.
articles.body: Water trapped deep beneath Gateshead is now helping heat hundreds of homes and public buildings, turning former coal mine workings into a source of heat for the city. The water lies around 150 metres below Gateshead town centre, where a 6-megawatt water-source heat pump extracts its heat and feeds it into an existing district heating network. According to the Mining Remediation Authority, the system went live on 29 March 2023 after about three years of work and is the largest mine water heat network in Great Britain. More than 5 kilometres of heat-network pipes carry the heat to buildings including Gateshead College, the Baltic Arts Centre, several offices and 350 council-owned homes. The network is also planned to reach another 270 privately owned homes, alongside a new conference centre and hotel development. The project is also being studied through the Gateshead Living Laboratory, where boreholes and monitoring equipment collect data on the mine water system.Mine water heat pump powers Gateshead buildingsA 6 megawatt water-source heat pump recovers heat from the mine water and transfers it into the district heating network. The heated water is then distributed through more than 5 kilometres of heat-network pipes to connected buildings.The network currently supplies heat to several types of buildings across Gateshead. These include Gateshead College, the Baltic Arts Centre, several offices and 350 council-owned homes. The source states that the system is also planned to serve another 270 privately owned homes, as well as a new conference centre and a hotel development.Why does mine water get warmer with depthMine water becomes warmer with increasing depth because of what the Mining Remediation Authority describes as a ‘geothermal gradient’. Mine water temperatures generally range from 10°C to 20°C, although they can reach 40°C at depths of around 1 kilometre. Water can be brought to the surface through boreholes, shafts or adits, before heat exchangers and pumps recover its heat. The authority says mine water temperatures are not affected by seasonal variations. It describes mine water as a potential source of “renewable, secure, low carbon heating for buildings in coalfield areas”, with the right support and sustainable management.What is the Gateshead living laboratory studyingThe Gateshead mine water heating network is part of a wider research project known as the Gateshead Living Laboratory. The initiative is designed to collect evidence that supports future licensing, management and wider use of mine water heat schemes. It is located near three mine water heat schemes in the North East of England.With support from Gateshead Council, researchers drilled four boreholes and installed monitoring equipment to gather data. The information is available as open-access data for researchers, regulators, stakeholders and academic institutions. The government says the work will help researchers study the thermal and hydrogeological interactions between multiple mine water heat schemes in the Walker mining block in Tyne and Wear.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
